title: Security hardening: headers, WAF rules, secret scanning, dependency policy
goal: Harden the platform's surface: security response headers and CORS, WAF and edge rate-limit rules, secret scanning, and a dependency policy enforced in CI, so common web attacks and supply-chain mistakes are caught automatically.
scope_in: Fastify plugin `securityHeaders` for the API: `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload`, `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-site`, `Permissions-Policy` empty, `Cache-Control: no-store` on `/v1/auth/*`, billing and other authenticated JSON by default.
CORS policy: allow only the web app origins from config (`CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`), no wildcard, credentials only for `/v1/auth/token` with the `X-Centcom-Client: web` header, preflight cache 600 s.

Edge WAF module `infra/terraform/modules/waf/`: managed rule sets, rate-limit rules mirroring CT-PAGE buckets (anonymous 30/min/IP, auth endpoints 20/min/IP), body-size limits (1 MiB on `/v1/usage/events`, 256 KiB elsewhere), blocked methods, bot rules for anonymous endpoints, WebSocket upgrade allow-list for the relay host.
Secret scanning: `.gitleaks.toml`, pre-commit hook and a CI workflow `security-scan.yml` (gitleaks on the diff and full history weekly).

Dependency policy enforced by `tools/security/`-style scripts under `infra/security/`: `check-deps.mjs` (no install scripts except allow-list, exact pins, `pnpm audit` fails on high/critical, lockfile integrity), `check-licenses.mjs` (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3, ISC only), CycloneDX SBOM per build, Renovate/Dependabot config with grouped weekly updates.
Container hardening checks: non-root user, read-only root filesystem where possible, distroless/slim base, trivy gate (fail on critical).
scope_out: Application-level authn/authz (B017-B021) and rate limiting middleware (B023).
Core CI pipeline (B002); this lane adds a separate workflow file and scripts.
Terraform of the rest of the infrastructure (B091).
build_against: A header-assertion test suite running against an in-process Fastify instance; WAF rules validated with `terraform validate`/plan JSON policy tests; dependency scripts run against the repo and fixtures containing deliberately bad packages.
interfaces: Fastify plugin `securityHeaders(opts: {allowedOrigins: string[]})` registered before routes.
Terraform module `waf` inputs: `zone_id`, `api_hostname`, `relay_hostnames`, `ws_path_regex`, `rate_limits`; outputs rule ids.
acceptance: Every API response (200, 304, 4xx, 5xx, preflight) carries the headers listed above; a table-driven test over 15 representative routes asserts exact values; authenticated and billing routes also carry `Cache-Control: no-store`.

A request with `Origin: https://evil.example` receives no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`; an allowed origin receives exactly that origin (not `*`) with `Vary: Origin`; credentials are allowed only on `/v1/auth/token`.
`pnpm security:secrets` fails on a planted fake AWS key and a planted `cen_live_` key in a test fixture, and passes on a clean tree; the weekly full-history scan job is defined.
`pnpm security:deps` fails for: a dependency with an install script not on the allow-list, a range (`^`/`~`) version, a high-severity advisory, a GPL licence; passes on the repo's real lockfile.
SBOM CycloneDX JSON is produced for each service image and attached to the CI run; trivy fails the build on critical findings in the image.
WAF plan JSON contains: managed ruleset enabled, rate-limit rules 30/min and 20/min as stated, body limits, and denies non-HTTPS; policy test asserts them.
Containers run as non-root (UID != 0) verified by a Dockerfile lint test; the WAF does not block the relay's WS upgrade on the allow-listed path (verified in a plan test of rule ordering).
tests: header table-driven tests (Vitest) incl. error paths.
script tests with fixture repos for deps, licences and secrets.
Terraform plan-JSON policy tests for the WAF module.
Dockerfile lint (hadolint) and trivy in CI.
regression test that `Cache-Control: no-store` is present on `/v1/auth/token`.
guardrails: MUST NOT use wildcard CORS origins and MUST NOT reflect arbitrary `Origin` values.
MUST NOT weaken a header per route without a documented exception list in `docs/security/hardening.md` and a test.
MUST NOT add runtime dependencies with install scripts; exceptions require an issue link and an allow-list entry with justification.
MUST NOT commit secrets scanning baselines that hide real findings; baseline entries need expiry dates.
MUST NOT block `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/v1/status` or the relay WS upgrade through WAF rules (availability).
failure_modes: WAF rule false positive blocks legitimate traffic -> rule can be switched to `log` mode via variable without redeploying the app; runbook entry.
Advisory database outage in CI -> `security:deps` fails closed on main, warns on PRs after 1 retry.
New dependency lacks licence metadata -> treated as failure until reviewed.
